data.note: Correctly called Protein degradation for proteasome inhibitor I (PubChem CID 16760625, BBBC021 annotation). NSC vote was unanimous 4/4 Protein degradation (e9) despite microscopist's Microtubule stabilizers call from bright bundled tubulin (e5,e6, tub_mean z=7-11, tub_glcm_contrast z=30 at 10uM). Discounting the blurry DMSO control and noting lack of mitotic enrichment (frac_mitotic_like negative, e15) and diffuse enlarged nuclei with decreased DNA mean/increased integrated intensity (e8,e11) supported proteasome block over true stabilization. Proteasome inhibition causes tubulin/centrosomal protein accumulation and altered microtubule organization (e.g. parkin recruitment to centrosome upon proteasome inhibition, PMID:12928331), explaining the microtubule-mimetic phenotype that confounded morphology alone. Follow-up: proteasome activity assay + ubiquitin aggregate staining vs reference inhibitor as proposed.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is proteasome inhibitor I (CID 16760625) - agent call of Protein degradation at p=0.58 was correct, and the scoring is appropriate given the conflict in the primary data.

What got it right: 
The quantitative nuclear signature was the most consistent driver. Across 0.03uM (e8), 0.3uM (e3) and 1uM (e7) we repeatedly saw enlarged/diffuse nuclei: nuc_dna_mean strongly negative (-6.0 to -7.6), nuc_dna_integrated strongly positive (+4.9 to +6.8) with increased nuc_area/eccentricity (e7 z=+11.8). This fits protein accumulation without condensation, not stabilization-driven arrest. In parallel, the reference atlas comparison was unanimous: NSC 2/2 (e4) then 4/4 (e9) for Protein degradation (similarities 0.49-0.60) despite k-neighbour noise (e9: Protein synthesis 4/10, Protein degradation 3/10). The final weighting in e13/e17 correctly down-weighted the visual call against this.

The critical negative evidence was mitotic status. Microtubule stabilizers should enrich mitotic-like figures in a dose-dependent way. Here frac_mitotic_like was depressed at all doses (z=-1.5 to -0.8) and dose_response rho=-0.26, p=0.74 (e15). That lack of enrichment, together with cell_count rho=-0.80 (e14) indicating loss of density noted visually in e5/e6, favors cytotoxic protein accumulation over cytostatic stabilization.

What misled and why:
The tubulin channel was misleading on first look. Well w_d128269dd7 at 10uM (e2): tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean z=+11.3, tub_std z=+9.7, and w_ad5942f01b (e3) tub_mean z=+7.6. Both microscopist reads (e5: 6 obs, e6: 7 obs) flagged candidates: Microtubule stabilizers. Proteasome inhibition can produce secondary tubulin brightening/bundling via centrosome/ubiquitinated protein aggregation, PMID 12928331, so the visual similarity is biologically plausible and not a pure artifact, though the review noted the DMSO comparator was blurred/out-of-focus, weakening that call.

Acquisition choice to sample 4 doses (e1: 0.003-10uM, 4 wells acquired) resolved this. The tubulin signal was non-monotonic and inconsistent: tub_mean rho=+0.40, p=0.6 (e10), tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.40, p=0.6 (e12), and at 1uM (e7) tub_glcm_contrast was 0.14 despite strong nuclear changes. A true stabilizer would show monotonic intensification and texture bundling; the unstable dose response contradicted it. Similarly nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.80 (e11) and frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 (e16) were not significant with n=4, p=0.2, so we did not over-interpret dose trends and relied on consistency across absolute z-scores instead.

What was missed/kept modest:
Probability 0.58 was appropriately modest. The atlas k-neighbours included Protein synthesis and DNA damage (e4: 3/10 DNA damage; e9: 4/10 Protein synthesis), and no ChEMBL curated mechanism was available at lookup (e19/e20), so reliance on NSC vote alone carried risk. The literature search (e21/e22) had not yet been used for orthogonal validation at submission. Next-experiment logic recorded - proteasome activity with fluorogenic chymotrypsin-like substrate plus ubiquitin/p53 aggregates and phospho-H3 mitotic index - remains the correct discriminating test in a real lab to separate degradation block from primary tubulin stabilization.

In short: the decision to trust unanimous NSC across doses plus absence of mitotic arrest and presence of enlarged diffuse nuclei outweighed a strong but dose-inconsistent tubulin brightening and visual stabilizer call that is confounded by proteasome-induced tubulin/centrosome effects.
